newsitem.title: ITALY: Anglican leader sounds alarm on divorce rate.
newsitem.headline: Anglican leader sounds alarm on divorce rate.

text.p: The leader of the world's Anglicans, Archbishop of Canterbury George Carey, sounded an alarm on Wednesday over the soaring divorce rate and its increasingly traumatic effects on children.

"The family is under attack in our so-called civilised societies from the cult of individualism and a cultural emphasis on self-fulfilment and instant gratification," Carey said in a lecture at a Christian unity centre in Rome.
Rapid economic and social changes and the concept that what is right is a matter of individual opinion had weakened the traditional bonds of civic society.
"Many marriages collapse and an increasing number of children are brought up in beleagured one-parent families," said Carey, who is on an official visit to the Vatican.
Carey said studies had shown that in Britain more than 50,000 children each year under the age of five have parents who divorce and that the figures were rising.

"If present trends continue in the U.K. four in 10 new marriages wil end in divorce. Even if many of these children settle down in new families we cannot assume that they will overcome the trauma of separation easily," Carey said.
Carey praised Pope John Paul for his efforts to defend the family, a concern he said he shared. Carey is spiritual leader of the 70 million member Anglican Communion.
In his speech at Rome's Pro-Unity Centre, Carey also argued that future generations would pass harsh judgment on the 20th century and the role of Christianity during its course.
Listing the tragedies of the century -- ranging from the Holocaust and two world wars to the crisis in Rwanda -- he said:
"We might be forgiven for thinking that 20th century humanity in general, and perhaps Christianity in particular, has failed."
Carey said he regretted that too much competition among denominations had taken place in the past, particularly in mission countries.

"All too often in the course of the Christian centuries has mission been misunderstood as a strategy for confessional expansionism rather than the internal imperative of a life lived in conformity with the gospel," Carey said.
"We have all too frequently retreated behind the walls of denominational conformity occasionally sending out raiding parties for scalps," he said.
